response.internal_assessment: This is no longer a rumor. Maria Santos made a public statement naming RoboRide — the council is mobilizing, two residents have already sold their cars, and the launch is in four weeks. I sent my memo to Sandra a month ago and I haven't gotten a substantive response. That silence tells me two things: either leadership doesn't share my urgency, or they're waiting for me to come back with harder numbers. Either way, I can't stay in a holding pattern waiting for permission to prepare. My role security is my real threat here — not my personal finances, which are solid — and the branch's auto loan concentration is the vulnerability. The question I'm sitting with this tick is whether I've crossed the threshold where I have not just the right but the professional obligation to begin adjusting branch behavior, not just analyzing it. I think I have.

chosen_actions.description: Send a follow-up communication to Sandra Okafor — not another memo, but a direct request for a 20-minute call this week. Reference the Maria Santos public statement and the RoboRide Phase 2 confirmation as the reason for urgency. Attach an updated scenario model with a third scenario added: 50% decline in auto loan origination over 18 months, reflecting a more aggressive adoption curve. Make clear I am ready to present a branch-level response plan if she wants one. Frame it as seeking alignment, not asking permission.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: 1.5 hours to update the scenario model and draft the follow-up. No financial cost. I am spending political capital by being persistent, but staying quiet now is the greater risk.
chosen_actions.reasoning: Sandra's non-response last tick may reflect organizational inertia, not disagreement. The Maria Santos statement is now a public fact — I'm no longer escalating a rumor. If I do nothing and the branch takes a hit, my earlier memo protects me somewhat, but only somewhat. A follow-up with harder numbers and a request for alignment is what a high-performing branch manager does. It also creates a second record that I was watching.

chosen_actions.description: Begin a quiet, procedurally sound tightening of new auto loan origination criteria at the margin. Specifically: raise the minimum credit score threshold for new unsecured auto loans by 10 points, shorten maximum loan terms from 72 months to 60 months on vehicles older than 3 years, and flag any new dealer floor plan renewal requests for enhanced review before approval. Do not announce this as a policy change — frame it internally as 'refreshed underwriting guidelines' consistent with the bank's general credit quality standards. Document the rationale as standard risk cycle management, not RoboRide-specific.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: 2 hours to draft and route the internal underwriting guidance update. No direct financial cost. This will likely reduce loan origination volume by 5-10% in the short term, which is an acceptable trade for reduced tail risk.
chosen_actions.reasoning: I now have public confirmation that a disruptive mobility service is deploying in 4 weeks. Vehicles financed today on 72-month terms will still be on our books when the local market for personal vehicle ownership has potentially shifted. Tightening at the margin is defensible, proportionate, and within my authority as branch manager. I am not punishing Rick or Patricia — I am managing credit risk, which is my job. The key is framing and documentation. I don't tighten based on RoboRide speculation; I tighten because extending long-duration credit on depreciating assets in a period of transportation market uncertainty is consistent with our standard risk appetite.

economic_effects.expected_portfolio_risk_reduction: reduced tail exposure on long-duration depreciating asset loans

chosen_actions.description: Call Patricia Hawkins at Regional Auto Group and Rick Hernandez for the direct conversation I couldn't have last tick. Maria's statement is now public — I don't need to protect a rumor source anymore. Open with: 'I know you've seen the council statement. I want to understand how you're thinking about the next 90 days, and I want to be straight with you about what we're watching on our end.' Listen for whether they're planning to adapt (inventory mix, service revenue emphasis, EV fleet pivots) or whether they're in denial. Their response directly informs whether I tighten further or hold. Strong adaptive clients are still creditworthy. Clients in denial are a leading indicator of future default.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: 1.5 hours for two substantive calls. No financial cost. High relationship and intelligence value.
chosen_actions.reasoning: Patricia and Rick are not just borrowers — they are the anchors of the branch's dealer relationships. I owe them honesty now that the situation is public. And frankly, their strategic response to this disruption will tell me more about their credit quality over the next 18 months than their last three years of financials. A dealer who is already thinking about how to adapt is a fundamentally different credit than one who is waiting for RoboRide to fail. I learn more in this conversation than from any internal model.

chosen_actions.description: Accelerate the commercial and small business lending continuing education to maximum pace — push from 10% completion to at least 35% this tick by dedicating 6 hours per week instead of the current rate. Specifically prioritize the SBA 7(a) loan product module and the section on service-sector small business underwriting. Begin identifying 3-5 existing branch relationships — non-auto, non-dealer clients — who might be good candidates for a commercial lending conversation within 60 days.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: Approximately 18-20 hours of focused study and identification work this tick. No financial cost. This is personal and professional investment.
chosen_actions.reasoning: RoboRide launches in 4 weeks. My certification progress at 10% is too slow given the timeline. The branch needs to demonstrate that it can originate and manage commercial and small business loans before auto loan volume decline shows up in the numbers — not after. If I can show Sandra a pipeline of commercial loan prospects alongside a managed auto portfolio, I am a branch manager who responded to disruption intelligently. If I show up in 6 months with a smaller auto book and no replacement pipeline, I am a manager who watched it happen. This training is now urgent, not optional.

chosen_actions.description: Open a discrete personal file — not shared, not in bank systems — that tracks my branch manager role risk explicitly. Write down my honest assessment: role security 0.36, auto loans are 60%+ of origination volume, launch in 4 weeks. Identify two specific contingency scenarios: (1) branch restructuring or consolidation within 18 months, requiring me to either move to a regional role or exit; (2) voluntary transition to commercial banking focus within the same bank if I build sufficient credentials in time. For each scenario, write down one concrete preparatory action I could take this month. This is not panic planning — it is the kind of honest self-assessment I would demand of any borrower asking me for a loan.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: 1 hour of focused private reflection and writing. No financial cost.
chosen_actions.reasoning: My status_quo_bias is 0.66 — I know I have a structural pull toward assuming things will stabilize. The purpose of this file is to counteract that bias by making the scenarios concrete and written. I am not acting on it yet. I am making the paths legible so that if I need to move, I move from a plan rather than from panic. A banker with $173K in savings and 24+ months of runway has the luxury of planning calmly. I should use that luxury now.

response.emotional_state: deliberate urgency — the situation has clarified and I am moving with precision, not speed for its own sake. Privately more unsettled than I show at work.
response.inner_monologue: I've been the most prepared person in the room for two months — I need to make sure that still means something when the launch actually hits.
